title: PRD: Standard Cost Model (SCM) Spec + Cost Model API
author: Talia Benson
body:
h1. Overview
Redwood Inference is standardizing how we model and expose inference cost so that *Console* (cost breakdown + transparency) and *Optimize* (recommendations and “what-if” analysis) operate on consistent, auditable economics across *Hosted*, *Dedicated*, and *Private* deployments.

This PRD defines:
* The problem and target users
* Product requirements for the Standard Cost Model (SCM) spec and a versioned Cost Model API
* Success metrics (accuracy bands, latency, adoption)
* Milestones and rollout plan

h1. Problem statement
Today, cost attribution and cost “estimates” are implemented inconsistently across services and deployment modes:
* Console cost pages rely on a mix of token metering, heuristic compute assumptions, and deployment-specific logic.
* Optimize needs a deterministic, comparable evaluator to recommend batching/caching/quantization changes without misleading customers.
* Runtime and telemetry expose signals (batching, caching, prefill/decode, quant profile) that are not normalized or consistently available across regions/SKUs.

As a result:
* Customers see discrepancies between “cost breakdown” and real behavior (especially when batching/caching changes).
* Internal teams cannot compare unit economics across model families, regions, or deployment modes without bespoke analysis.
* Support escalations are hard to resolve because we cannot provide an explainable, auditable breakdown.

h1. Goals
h2. Primary goals
1) Define a *Standard Cost Model (SCM)* spec with canonical inputs/outputs, units, and semantics.
2) Ship a *versioned Cost Model API* that provides deterministic results for:
   * *Estimate*: what the cost would be given a workload/config.
   * *Explain/Attribution*: why cost is what it is, with a clear breakdown and confidence/assumptions.
3) Align runtime telemetry signals with SCM so attribution is explainable and comparable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
4) Provide guardrails: backward compatibility policy, validation rules, audit logging, and SLOs.

h2. Non-goals (initial release)
* Do *not* change customer billing or invoice source-of-truth.
* Do *not* build a full pricing/discount engine. SCM models *technical cost attribution* and consistent estimates; contract terms remain separate.

h1. Target users and use-cases
h2. Primary users (internal)
* *Console Engineering / Product* (Marissa Cole, Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams)
  * Display estimated cost breakdowns per model/route/tenant.
  * Show transparent assumptions and confidence.
  * Provide “why did this change?” context for deltas.

* *Optimize Engineering / Product* (Aditya Rao, Hassan Mirza, Yara Haddad)
  * Run “what-if” scenario sweeps for candidate configs:
    * batching on/off; batch size targets
    * cache warm vs cold
    * quantization profile swap
  * Produce recommendations with guardrails (do not recommend with low confidence).

h2. Secondary users
* *SRE/Infra* (Sean Gallagher, Neha Kapoor, Rafael Mendes): reliability targets, runbooks, dashboards.
* *Telemetry platform* (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman): dimension standards and cardinality controls.
* *Security/Compliance* (Dr. Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei): auditability of access to customer cost data.
* *Support/CS*: interpretability for customer questions and escalations.

h2. Representative user stories
1) Console breakdown:
   *As a Console user*, I can view total estimated cost for a route/model over a time window, with a breakdown (compute/memory/cache effects) and clear assumptions/confidence, so I can understand cost drivers.

2) Optimize what-if:
   *As an Optimize user*, I can run a “what-if” comparison between current config and a proposed config (e.g., enable prefix caching + adjust batching), and get a cost delta with confidence and stated assumptions.

3) Support explainability:
   *As Support*, I can pull an explain payload that indicates whether an estimate relied on defaults due to missing telemetry, and which signals contributed most, so I can respond to discrepancy reports.

h1. Product requirements
h2. SCM specification (v1)
The SCM v1 spec must define:
* Canonical *inputs* (required vs optional)
* Canonical *outputs* (total + breakdown)
* Units and normalization across hardware SKUs and deployment modes
* Deterministic calculation rules
* Explicit assumptions and confidence semantics

h3. Inputs (v1)
Required inputs (hard validation failure if missing):
* deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
* model_id and model_version (or an immutable model catalog reference)
* region (logical region used by routing/infra)
* hardware_sku (or resolvable via model catalog + deployment)
* tokens: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens (or prefill/decode token counts when available)
* request shape: max_sequence_length (or equivalent constraint used in runtime)

Optional inputs (accepted when available; required for higher confidence):
* prefill_tokens, decode_tokens split (if different from prompt/completion semantics)
* batch_size_effective and/or batch_efficiency
* kv_cache_hit_rate (and cache_mode)
* quant_profile_id and quant_profile_metadata (if not resolvable)
* concurrency/throughput hints (Optimize use-case)

h3. Outputs (v1)
Outputs must include:
* total_cost (currency-agnostic “cost units” for internal economics) and an optional currency mapping for display
* breakdown components (e.g., compute_cost, memory_cost, cache_savings, overhead)
* assumptions[]: explicit list of defaults applied (e.g., “kv_cache_hit_rate defaulted to 0 due to missing telemetry”)
* confidence: a normalized score/category (e.g., high/medium/low) with reasons
* contributing_factors[]: top drivers suitable for Console tooltips (bounded size)

Notes:
* Console and Optimize must treat low-confidence outputs as *informational only* and degrade gracefully.

h2. Cost Model API
h3. API endpoints (v1)
* POST /v1/cost-model:estimate
* POST /v1/cost-model:explain

Both endpoints:
* Require authn/authz via standard internal service-to-service and Console/Optimize service identities.
* Must be deterministic given the same request payload and resolved catalog metadata.
* Must support version negotiation (see Versioning section).

h3. Determinism and caching
* The service must produce stable results: same inputs => same outputs.
* Any dynamic tables (e.g., hardware normalization coefficients) must be versioned and referenced in responses.
* The service may cache responses, but caching must not change correctness (keyed by full normalized request + negotiated version).

h3. Validation and error model
* Strict schema validation for required fields.
* Explicit error codes that allow clients to distinguish:
  * Unsupported SCM version
  * Invalid/missing required inputs
  * Temporarily unavailable dependencies (e.g., model catalog)
* For *optional* telemetry signals, compute must proceed with documented defaults and lower confidence.

h2. Telemetry alignment requirements
Runtime + telemetry pipeline must emit/preserve the signals needed by SCM with cardinality controls:
* prefill/decode split counters
* batch_size_effective and batch_efficiency
* kv-cache hit rate
* quant_profile_id
* region and hardware_sku (or resolvable)

Constraints:
* Overhead budget: instrumentation must not materially regress runtime latency/throughput.
* Cardinality: dimensions must be bounded (e.g., quant_profile_id is enumerated; route/model identifiers are controlled; no raw prompt content).

h2. Console integration requirements
Console backend must:
* Call SCM for breakdown payloads powering cost pages.
* Implement safe fallbacks:
  * If SCM is unavailable or slow, show partial/previous values with “estimated” + “data unavailable” messaging.
  * Do not block core Console navigation on SCM.
* Cache appropriately to reduce SCM read load during dashboard refresh.

h2. Optimize integration requirements
Optimize pipeline must:
* Support scenario sweeps (N candidate configs) without overloading SCM.
  * Preferred: client-side batching with concurrency limits; a multi-scenario API is explicitly out-of-scope for v1 unless needed for performance.
* Apply guardrails:
  * Do not surface recommendations when confidence is below threshold.
  * Always attach assumptions to recommendations.

h2. Security, privacy, and audit logging
* Access to customer-level cost breakdown data is considered customer-sensitive for audit purposes.
* All reads of explain/attribution endpoints must emit audit events including:
  * actor (service + human if applicable via Console)
  * tenant/org
  * request scope (route/model/time window)
  * response classification (high/medium/low confidence)
  * redaction rules: never log prompt content; avoid high-cardinality identifiers beyond approved fields

h1. Success metrics
h2. Accuracy and explainability
Because SCM is not billing source-of-truth in v1, we measure *agreement* and *stability* rather than “invoice correctness.”

Definitions:
* *Metered attribution*: attribution derived from runtime telemetry for actual requests.
* *Estimate*: what SCM predicts for a given request shape/config.

Targets (v1 launch readiness):
* On a fixed canary prompt set per model family, SCM estimate vs metered attribution:
  * p50 absolute percent error <= 5%
  * p95 absolute percent error <= 15%
  * Any model-family outliers documented with known assumptions and tracked follow-ups
* Confidence calibration:
  * For requests missing key optional signals (kv-cache hit rate, batch signals), confidence must degrade to medium/low with explicit assumptions.

h2. API performance and reliability
Targets (for steady-state, per region):
* Availability: >= 99.9% monthly (excluding planned maintenance)
* Latency:
  * p95 <= 150ms for estimate
  * p95 <= 250ms for explain
  * p99 <= 500ms for both
* Error rate: <= 0.2% (5xx) excluding client validation failures

h2. Adoption
* Console:
  * 100% of internal tenants on SCM-backed cost breakdown within 2 weeks of GA
  * 50% of external Hosted tenants enabled (feature-flagged) within 4 weeks of GA
* Optimize:
  * 100% of Optimize “what-if” evaluations use SCM outputs for cost deltas within 2 weeks of GA

h1. Scope and phased delivery
h2. Phase 1: Discovery + alignment (Week 1–2)
Deliverables:
* Finalize terminology and units (compute vs memory vs cache savings)
* Confirm required runtime/telemetry signals and identify gaps
* Agree on “estimate” vs “metered attribution” boundary

Owners: Priya Natarajan (platform), Mateo Alvarez (runtime), Logan Wright (telemetry), Marissa Cole + Aditya Rao (product)

h2. Phase 2: Spec + ADRs (Week 2–3)
Deliverables:
* SCM v1 spec (schema + examples)
* ADR: versioning and negotiation (header vs path vs payload)
* API conventions: error model, idempotency requirements

h2. Phase 3: Implementation (Week 3–6)
Deliverables:
* Cost Model service skeleton + deterministic calculation engine
* Model catalog integration for resolving hardware SKU and quant profile metadata
* Runtime instrumentation hooks + telemetry pipeline updates
* Unit tests + golden test vectors for determinism

h2. Phase 4: Integrations (Week 6–8)
Deliverables:
* Console wiring + UI mapping (including assumptions/confidence copy)
* Optimize “what-if” sweep integration + guardrails
* Staging integration tests and load tests

h2. Phase 5: Launch (Week 8–10)
Deliverables:
* Staged rollout (internal -> canary -> wider)
* Dashboards/alerts + oncall runbooks
* Documentation + enablement for Support/CS

h1. Rollout plan
h2. Feature flags and progressive delivery
* cost_model_api_enabled: controls service routing for clients
* console_scm_breakdown_enabled: enables Console to call SCM and show SCM-backed breakdowns
* optimize_scm_enabled: enables Optimize scenario evaluation with SCM

Rollout steps:
1) Internal enablement (Redwood employees / dogfood tenants)
   * Validate payloads, copy, and confidence behavior
2) Canary tenants (small subset of Hosted + one Dedicated environment)
   * Compare SCM estimates vs metered attribution on canary prompt sets
   * Confirm no Console page-level degradation during timeouts
3) Expand by tier
   * Hosted: ramp by tenant cohort + region
   * Dedicated: ramp by cluster
   * Private: enable after validating required telemetry availability and audit constraints per customer

h2. Go/no-go criteria
* SLO dashboards green for 7 consecutive days in canary
* No P0/P1 incidents attributable to SCM in canary period
* Accuracy bands meet targets for top 5 models by traffic; outliers documented + confidence rules verified
* Security sign-off on audit events and redaction

h1. Dependencies
* Telemetry pipeline updates to preserve required dimensions with cardinality controls
* Model catalog integration for hardware_sku + quant profile metadata
* Runtime instrumentation: prefill/decode counters, batch efficiency, KV-cache hit rate
* API gateway routing + authn/authz policies
* SRE dashboards/alerts and runbooks

h1. Risks and mitigations
* Risk: Missing telemetry in certain deployments (especially Private) yields misleading output.
  * Mitigation: strict required inputs; explicit assumptions and confidence downgrades; deployment readiness checklist.

* Risk: Cardinality explosion from tagging (route/model/quant profile).
  * Mitigation: enumerated dimensions, aggregation rules, and review with observability standards.

* Risk: Console degradation if SCM is slow/unavailable.
  * Mitigation: client timeouts, caching, partial rendering, and fallbacks; SLO-based alerting.

* Risk: Customers interpret SCM as billing.
  * Mitigation: Console copy must label values as “estimated”; Support enablement; ensure SCM is not used for invoices until explicitly approved.

h1. Open questions
1) Should we add a first-class batch “multi-scenario” endpoint for Optimize, or standardize client-side batching limits?
2) What is the long-term plan for mapping internal “cost units” to currency display across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
3) How do we version and roll forward hardware normalization coefficients without breaking determinism guarantees for old responses?

h1. Appendix: Definitions
* *SCM (Standard Cost Model)*: a standardized schema and semantics for inference cost estimation and attribution.
* *Estimate*: cost prediction based on workload/config inputs, possibly using defaults.
* *Explain/Attribution*: a breakdown and reasons, including which signals and assumptions were used.
* *Confidence*: a normalized indicator of how complete/representative the input signals are for cost estimation.
